clue.text: Husband's chuckling is a crime

parts.note: a husband is a man, and the possessive keeps its S
chuckling is laughter

explanation.surface: A wife complains that her husband's giggling ought to be against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after its fourth letter and it reads as a man's laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Manslaughter is the legal offence of killing someone without malice aforethought.

clue.text: Proper side of expert seen in alternative to Skype

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or proper
a facet is one flat side of a cut gem
taken as written
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist's best feature shows up on a video call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side of expert' looks like a single idea, but side and expert are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting together in person is the low-tech substitute for a video-calling service.

clue.text: Rising ingredients of pastry fill unbearable void

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read from bottom to top
ingredients are contained in the dish, so the letters sit inside these words

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of pastry, all of fill and the start of unbearable

explanation.surface: Pastry rising badly leaves a dreadful empty space inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To void a contract is to annul it, making it have no legal force.

clue.text: Tradition in Russia: no noisy glasses

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional knowledge

indicators.note: noisy says we go by how these words sound when spoken, not how they are spelt

parts.note: nyet is Russian for no

explanation.surface: A Russian custom bans clinking glasses loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'lore nyet' approximates the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held up by a long handle rather than worn.

clue.text: A burp: novel, miraculous, like the existence of God

indicators.note: a miracle transforms things, so these letters take on a new order

parts.note: taken as written, letters for the anagram
taken as written: the word novel is part of the fodder, not a signal

explanation.surface: A theologian treats an unusual belch as a wonder pointing to the divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'miraculous' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Philosophers argue that God's existence cannot be demonstrated by proof either way.

clue.text: Actor's pain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: William ... or John ..., film actors
second meaning: ... as physical or emotional suffering

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Oscar-winning star doubles as the everyday word for injury or suffering.

clue.text: Message about the author's fabric riding up

indicators.note: in a down clue, riding up means the letters run from bottom to top
about means going round, so the fabric surrounds the author

parts.note: lamé is a fabric woven with metallic threads
the setter refers to themselves, giving I

explanation.surface: A note complaining that the writer's clothing keeps riding up.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is a message sent between computers.

clue.text: Postpone first bit of seasoning for fish

indicators.note: to postpone is to put off till later, so the opening letter is moved further back in the word

parts.note: spices season food
the first bit of the seasoning word is its opening S

explanation.surface: A cook delays adding seasoning to the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the opening S of the seasoning word moves, two places along.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisces is the zodiac sign of the Fishes, so the word itself is Latin for fish.

clue.text: Pauper shot stare of dislike

parts.note: a have-not is a poor person

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor man glares with obvious contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stare of dislike' reads as one phrase, but 'stare of' is the fodder and 'dislike' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any relish for something is a way of saying one finds it unpleasant.

clue.text: Mathematician's fuel ship in sound

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is the mathematician himself

indicators.note: in sound means we want a word spoken like the ship's name, not spelt like it

parts.note: an oiler is a tanker that carries fuel oil

explanation.surface: A puzzling claim that some mathematician owns a tanker for fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Leonhard Euler's surname is pronounced 'oiler', which is the whole trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician of enormous output.

clue.text: Caper stew with bread for each person

indicators.note: a stew is a jumble cooked together, so the word before it gets its letters mixed

parts.note: taken as written, the letters stewed
pita is a flat Middle Eastern bread

explanation.surface: A recipe portion: caper stew served with bread, one helping per diner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase per capita means by heads, that is, per individual.

clue.text: Tennis fan who offers legal advice?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tennis is played on a court
second meaning: an amicus curiae, a non-party who advises a court on a point of law

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful first reading; the second is the literal English for amicus curiae.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicus curiae is the Latin legal term for an outsider who submits advice to a court in a case.

clue.text: Celsius variation in Chile, for example — hot enough for you?

indicators.note: a variation is a rearranged version, so the letters given before and after it are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written, the country's name supplies its letters

explanation.surface: A weather report on temperature changes across Chile, ending with a sweaty quip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' tells you the definition is a sample of the kind of thing meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking 'Hot enough for you?' on a sweltering day is a worn-out stock remark, a classic platitude.

clue.text: Superlatively formal holy men flanking Veronica's friend

parts.note: ST, for saint, twice
Archie Andrews, Veronica Lodge's boyfriend in the Archie comics

explanation.surface: Two very proper priests escort a comic-book character.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy means stiff and formal in manner, and this is its superlative form.

clue.text: Weep outside of parent's vault

parts.note: to weep is to cry

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two end letters, so only the first and last of parent are kept

parts.note: only the outside letters of parent are used, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: Someone sobbing outside their mother's or father's burial vault.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after parent reads as 'is', a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground vault or chamber, typically beneath a church, used for burial.

clue.text: Like to paint abstractly at first, for a starter

indicators.note: abstract art departs from the literal form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: as means like, as in 'quick as lightning'
taken as written, letters for the anagram

explanation.surface: Advice to a beginning artist: try painting in an abstract style first.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian course of cold meats and pickles served before the main meal.

clue.text: Basic proposition in clipper at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters scrambled

explanation.surface: A fundamental claim about life aboard a sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A clipper is a fast sailing ship, which makes 'at sea' fit the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle is a fundamental truth or law serving as the foundation for reasoning.

clue.text: Migrant bank employee takes back most of change

indicators.note: the teller takes something in, so the other piece goes inside it

parts.note: a teller handles cash at a bank counter

indicators.note: back says the piece it governs is read in the reverse direction
most of a word drops its final letter

parts.note: to change is to vary

explanation.surface: An immigrant bank clerk keeps back some of the customers' coins.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the British spelling with two Ls, which the cross-reference from 18 down confirms.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller is anyone on a journey, and a migrant is one who moves from place to place.

clue.text: A second-rate thoroughfare, where a 17 might be

parts.note: taken as written
B is the grade below A
a road is a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A minor road, the kind where a wanderer turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is the traveller, someone typically away in another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a foreign country is the natural state of someone on a long journey.

clue.text: Gandhi abjures resistance for The Nation

indicators.note: to abjure is to renounce, so the letter standing for resistance is given up from the name

parts.note: Indira Gandhi, the twentieth-century prime minister, supplies her first name

explanation.surface: A former prime minister turns from passive resistance to serve the magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nation is the name of the magazine running this puzzle; here it is a country instead. R is the physics symbol for resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country, and a country is a nation, the capitals being a joke on the publisher's title.

clue.text: How to turn a tire into something to wear (a garment)

definitions.text: How to turn a tire into something to wear
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: double the T, which turns 'a tire' into 'attire'
second meaning: a close-fitting Renaissance jacket

explanation.surface: A puzzle about turning a car tyre into clothing, with a garment in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, an instruction: double the T. The bracketed part is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting man's jacket of the Renaissance period.

clue.text: Precede in favor of self

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
the ego is the self

explanation.surface: Choosing to go first out of sheer self-interest.
explanation.definitionFit: To forego, with an E, is an old sense meaning to go before or come earlier.

clue.text: Sparkle and spangle amid cargo

parts.note: the letters run across the end of spangle and the start of amid

explanation.surface: Glittering sequins packed in a ship's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief flash or glint of light, much like a sparkle.

clue.text: See 11
Loudly search for Indian believer

parts.note: to search for is to seek

clue.text: Truce in argument about error with cashier

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the argument goes round the error

parts.note: a case is the argument made by one side
E is the baseball scorer's mark for an error
to cashier is to dismiss from service, to fire

explanation.walkthrough: 'cashier' looks like a till worker but is a verb meaning to sack.

clue.text: Rice course with pass/fail mix-up

indicators.note: a mix-up jumbles things, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the grade letter for a pass on a pass/fail transcript
taken as written, the letters jumbled with P

explanation.walkthrough: Rice is a university in Houston, so the surface is about classes; the definition wants rice the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaf is a dish of rice cooked in seasoned broth, served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Band's equipment collided with radiator in auditorium

a radiator is a heater

explanation.surface: A band's gear crashed into the heating in the concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheater is a large tiered venue for audiences, so an arena-like auditorium.
